resources.string: Nothing needs your attention right now.
PermSense checks your apps every 15 minutes and will tell you if something looks wrong.
PermSense can only see which apps are installed and what they are allowed to do. To also see what apps actually do, set up the deeper checks in Settings.
Turn on “Usage access” for PermSense so it can tell when an app was on screen. Without it, PermSense can still list what apps are allowed to do, but cannot judge whether an access was hidden.
The private record on this phone could not be opened: %1$s
The saved record failed its self-check, so some findings may be missing. You can erase it in Settings and start fresh.
Shizuku is running, but PermSense has not been allowed to use it yet.
Live watch is paused. This is normal after your phone restarts: open Shizuku and start it again. PermSense keeps checking every 15 minutes in the meantime.
Live watch is off, so PermSense sees what apps are allowed to do, but only part of what they actually do. You can turn it on in setup.
PermSense is still learning what is normal for each of your apps. Unusual-activity checks get better over the first week or two.
Some rules are still waiting for a person to review them (%1$s). Their wording may change.
Apps you installed, with the sensitive things each one is allowed to use.
Lending apps are held to stricter rules, such as not reading contacts.
This app is no longer installed. Its history is kept until it ages out.
Older activity is kept only as daily totals.
Each change was checked afterwards. You can undo any of them.
You haven’t changed anything through PermSense.
PermSense will remove “%1$s” access from “%2$s”. You can undo this from the Summary tab. The app may not work properly without it.
PermSense will let “%2$s” use your %1$s only while the app is open. You can undo this from the Summary tab.
Done. Android now shows this access as removed.
Android did not apply the change.
The report could not be created.
Everything PermSense had stored has been erased.
Done. PermSense now holds %1$d permission(s) for itself.
To change permissions from here PermSense needs Shizuku. Opening the app’s settings page instead.
Set a screen lock on your phone first, then try again.
This phone has no app that can open that.
Asks for your fingerprint, face or screen lock each time you open it. It also hides PermSense from screenshots and the recent apps list.
Once a week, a short neutral note that your summary is ready. It never names an app.
The Exit button closes PermSense at once and removes it from the recent apps list.
Needs Shizuku. Sees each access as it happens. When off, PermSense only checks every 15 minutes.
Never use the broad DUMP permission
Skips the phone-history backfill. The permission it needs can read many system services, not only app permissions.
Press the button to try each kind of check and see which ones work here.

Creates a signed file and a readable report of what PermSense recorded. It proves the record was not changed after it was written. It does not prove that what Android reported was true, and PermSense makes no claim that it will be accepted in any legal proceeding.
Deletes the private record, its keys and every exported file from this phone. This cannot be undone.
This deletes everything PermSense has recorded on this phone, and its keys. Reports you already shared stay with whoever you gave them to. This cannot be undone.
PermSense has no internet access at all, and anyone can check that in the app’s permissions. Nothing leaves this phone unless you share a report yourself.

A report proves that the record was not changed after PermSense wrote it. It does not prove that the information Android gave PermSense was true. Someone with full control of the phone could, in principle, change entries before they are recorded.
PermSense makes no claim that any report will be accepted in any legal proceeding.
Some rules, including the lending rules, cite regulations whose exact clause numbers still need to be confirmed by a person.
Integrity check of the record: passed
Integrity check of the record: FAILED
Use your fingerprint, face or screen lock
A short note when there is something new to look at.
Once a week, a short summary of your apps.
PermSense watches how your apps use their permissions (contacts, camera, microphone, location and more) and tells you, in plain words, when something looks wrong.
Everything stays on this phone. PermSense has no internet access at all.
It only watches. It changes nothing unless you press a button and confirm.
Setup takes a few minutes. Only the next step is needed; the rest is optional.
This lets PermSense see when an app was open on your screen. That is how it tells an access you could see from one you could not.
In the list, find PermSense and switch it on, then come back here.
PermSense can send a short, neutral note when something needs a look, and a weekly summary. Notifications never name an app and are hidden on the lock screen.
Without this step PermSense lists what every app can use. With it, PermSense also sees what apps actually do and when, even in the background. It needs a helper app called Shizuku.
Shizuku is not installed. Install it from its official page, then come back here.
Shizuku is installed but not running. Open it and start it with “Wireless debugging” (Android 11 or later). Android will show a pairing code once.
After every restart of your phone, Shizuku must be started again. That is normal, not a fault. PermSense keeps working in the meantime, with fewer details.
Shizuku is running. Allow PermSense to use it.
Shizuku is running and PermSense is allowed to use it.
On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones, also switch on “USB debugging (Security settings)”. It is a separate switch from ordinary USB debugging.
On OPPO, Realme and OnePlus phones, switch off “Permission monitoring” in Developer options before starting Shizuku.
Phone makers sometimes add their own switch for debugging. If a step here seems to do nothing, look in Developer options for an extra debugging switch, and see Shizuku’s own guide for your brand.
Phone makers sometimes add their own switch for debugging. If a step here seems to do nothing, look in Developer options for an extra debugging switch, and see Shizuku’s own guide for your brand.
Phone makers sometimes add their own switch for debugging. If a step here seems to do nothing, look in Developer options for an extra debugging switch, and see Shizuku’s own guide for your brand.
Gives PermSense a few Android permissions, once, so its 15-minute checks keep working after a restart even when Shizuku is off. After this you can switch developer options off again.
Done. The checks will keep working after a restart.
This needs Shizuku to be running and allowed first.
Skip the phone-history backfill, so the broad DUMP permission is never asked for or used.
Some banking apps refuse to run while developer options are on. Once the permissions above are given, you can switch developer options off again.
Here is what works on this phone. You can change any of this later in Settings.
